rows.note: Use 已故 as the all-purpose adjective for someone who is deceased, especially in formal or written contexts.

example.english: The works of the dead writer Jin Yong are still very popular today.
example.traditional: 已故作家金庸嘅作品，至今仍然好受歡迎。
example.jyutping: ji5 gu3 zok3 gaa1 gam1 jung4 ge3 zok3 ban2 zi3 gam1 jing4 jin4 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4

rows.note: Use 攰 for the adjective meaning exhausted, with the context showing that the tiredness is extreme.

example.english: I was dead tired after moving house today.
example.traditional: 我今日搬完屋，真係攰到郁唔到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 bun1 jyun4 uk1 zan1 hai6 gui6 dou3 juk1 m4 dou2

rows.note: Use 冇電 when a device or circuit is dead specifically because it has no power, not merely because it has no signal.

example.english: My phone is dead and won't turn on.
example.jyutping: bou6 din6 waa2 mou5 din6 hoi1 m4 dou2 gei1

rows.note: Use 死梗 when someone is doomed or in serious trouble, often as a threatening prediction.

example.english: If you don't leave now, you're dead when they catch you!
example.traditional: 你再唔走，畀人捉到就死梗喇！
example.jyutping: nei5 zoi3 m4 zau2 bei2 jan4 zuk1 dou2 zau6 sei2 gang2 laa3
